transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here because... after I eat too much, I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom. I do it so I won't gain weight, but it's gotten to the point where I'm honestly scared I can't stop doing it.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how that compares to what's typical for you?

Honestly, I'm not entirely sure what my exact weight is right now. I try to avoid getting on the scale because it just... it messes with my head too much. As for my height, I haven't been measured in years. 

I know my weight probably fluctuates a bit with all the throwing up, but my work uniforms still fit about the same as they always have at the shop. So I think I'm probably close to whatever is normal for me, I just don't have the actual numbers to give you.
When you say you 'eat too much' before purging, can you describe what that's like—do you feel like you can't control or stop the eating once you start?

Yeah, that's exactly what it is. Once I start on those nights, it's like my hands just keep grabbing food. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Lucy, knock it off,' I just can't seem to stop. I really don't feel back in charge of myself until it's already done and the food is gone.
How often would you say these episodes of overeating followed by vomiting happen—like, how many times per week—and how long has this pattern been going on?

It's been going on for at least the past three months now. There’s... well, there's hardly been a week in that time where I didn’t have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. 

As for how many times a week, it depends. Some weeks it happens several times... especially when my back is acting up and I’m stuck at home resting instead of working at the shop.
Would you say that your sense of self-worth or how you feel about yourself is heavily tied to your weight or body shape?

Yeah, I'd say it is. It's... well, it's pretty bad. Like, if my work pants feel tight when I put them on, or if I happen to catch a glimpse of my belly in the mirror, it just ruins everything. I start feeling like I'm failing at life. It makes me feel like I'm not that strong woman who used to haul transmissions around and keep right up with the guys at the shop. It just takes over how I see myself entirely.
